records.name: Nicetown CDC
records.summary: A community development group for the Nicetown neighborhood. Each summer it runs a neighborhood festival that needs volunteers, and it lists land care, arts and empowerment programs.
records.what_you_do: Sign up to volunteer for the Give Back Festival in August. The volunteer link opens a third-party sign-in page, so the office phone is the other way in. The site also lists a same-day work day and land care work, but how to join those is not shown.

schedule.text: Give Back Festival on August 7 and 8, 2026. Work days and program meetings are not shown on the site.

cost.text: Cost of volunteering is not stated

first_step.how: Use the Give Back Festival volunteer link on the group's site (it opens a sign-in page), or call the office
first_step.basis: Festival volunteering is public and the office phone is listed, but the sign-up page needs a third-party login

records.notes: Festival dates come from the home page. Most other dated news on the site is from 2023.

records.name: Mt. Airy CDC
records.summary: A community development group for Mt. Airy that offers housing counseling and runs neighborhood events. Neighbors can sign up through its volunteer link to help.
records.what_you_do: Sign up through the volunteer link to help with neighborhood events. Current events include Autumn on the Avenue, a trick-or-treat walk at local shops on Germantown Avenue on October 22, and a first-time homebuyer workshop on Thursdays in October 2026.

schedule.text: First-time homebuyer workshop on Thursdays October 8, 15 and 22, 2026, 5:30 to 8:30 pm. Autumn on the Avenue on Thursday October 22 (time not shown).

first_step.how: Use the volunteer link on the home page, or sign up on the event page for the homebuyer workshop
first_step.basis: Volunteer sign-up and event pages are public and linked from the home page

records.notes: The volunteer and events pages were linked from the home page but not opened. The Autumn on the Avenue year is not written on the page, so that date is not dated here.

records.name: Chestnut Hill Business District
records.summary: The business district group for Chestnut Hill and the Germantown Avenue shops. It runs volunteer clean-ups in the neighborhood parks and streets and hosts seasonal events.
records.what_you_do: Join a volunteer clean-up: the Friends of Pastorius Park fall clean-up on Saturday October 24, 2026 (9 am to noon, rain date the next day), or the Cresheim Valley Drive clean-up on Saturday October 17 (9 am to noon). The page does not say how to sign up, so ask through the listed contacts.

schedule.text: Volunteer clean-ups on Saturday mornings in October: Pastorius Park on October 24, 2026, 9 am to noon (rain date Sunday October 25), and Cresheim Valley Drive on Saturday October 17, 9 am to noon.

cost.text: Cost of joining a clean-up is not stated

first_step.how: Contact the district by phone or email to sign up for a clean-up
first_step.basis: Clean-ups are posted publicly, but the page does not say how to sign up

records.notes: PACDC lists this group as Chestnut Hill CDC. Its own site calls it the Chestnut Hill Business District, so the record uses that name and keeps the old one as an alias. The Cresheim Valley clean-up line gives no year, so it is not dated.

records.name: New Kensington CDC
records.summary: A neighborhood group for Kensington, Port Richmond and Fishtown that works on jobs, housing and safer blocks. It runs a weekend gardening club and helps neighbors form neighborhood associations.
records.what_you_do: Join the Weekend Gardening Club (listed for October 10, 2026, 10 am), find or start a neighborhood association through the group's neighborhood associations page, or come to a listed community meeting such as the Kensington Business Coalition meeting on October 13, 2026, 10 am. Friday drop-in hours with Cure Violence Kensington are also listed.

schedule.text: Weekend Gardening Club on October 10, 2026 at 10 am. Kensington Business Coalition meeting on October 13, 2026 at 10 am. Cure Violence Kensington drop-in hours on Friday October 9, 2026 at 2 pm.

first_step.how: Come to a listed event, or call the office to ask about the gardening club or a neighborhood association
first_step.basis: Events are posted with dates and times, and a public phone line is listed

records.notes: The www host has a certificate error, so the record uses nkcdc.org. The Community Health Worker parent workshops are dated May with no year and are left out. The volunteer and events pages were not opened.

records.name: East Falls Development Corporation
records.summary: The development group for East Falls, focused on the Riverfront Business District and Conrad Street. Neighbors can help at the fall East Falls Fest, join its committees, or help the River Landing friends group.
records.what_you_do: Help at the East Falls Fest on Saturday October 17, 2026 (11 am to 5 pm, along Ridge and Midvale), or sign up to volunteer or vend by email. The East Falls River Landing Friends Group looks after the riverfront access site and is reached through its own Facebook page or the group's email.

schedule.text: East Falls Fest on Saturday October 17, 2026, 11 am to 5 pm, along Ridge and Midvale. Committee and friends-group meeting times are not shown.

first_step.how: Email the group to sign up to volunteer for the fest or to join a committee
first_step.basis: Volunteer and vendor sign-up is public with a listed email; committee steps are not shown

records.notes: The fest year comes from the event page. The home page's flood-planning item is dated 2022. The fest volunteer contact is a named staff email on the event page; the record uses the general address instead.

records.name: Philadelphia Chinatown Development Corporation
records.summary: A community development group for Chinatown that runs housing, counseling, youth and planning programs and the Crane Community Center. Neighbors can volunteer for events and help with translation.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer for events, or offer translation and interpretation, which is an ongoing need. Volunteer forms are posted on social media, and the newsletter is the other way to hear about them; for translation, email or call. Crane Community Center membership costs $80 a year for an individual. The site also names a Neighborhood Advisory Committee and youth programming, with no join steps shown.

schedule.text: Events are listed on the group's events page. Volunteer and committee meeting times are not shown.

cost.text: Volunteering is free. Crane Community Center membership is $80 a year for an individual.

first_step.how: Sign up for the newsletter or follow the group on social media to hear about volunteer forms; email the office for translation work
first_step.basis: Volunteer sign-up is public, but the way in runs through a newsletter or social post

records.notes: The Get Involved page says volunteer forms are posted on social media. The Neighborhood Advisory Committee and youth programs have no join steps on the site.

records.name: Germantown United CDC
records.summary: A community development group for Germantown. It cleans up commercial corridors, adds trash cans, runs resident advisory committees and hosts community gatherings such as For the Love of Germantown.
records.what_you_do: The site lists a Neighborhood Advisory Committee and a Neighborhood Advisory Subcommittee for residents, plus Corridor Cleaning and Germantown Grows Together. How to join them is not shown; the get-involved page is the next place to look.

schedule.text: Office hours are Monday to Friday, 9 am to 5:30 pm, by appointment. Committee meeting times are not shown.

first_step.how: Call the office by appointment, or use the get-involved page to ask about the resident committees
first_step.basis: The committees are named, but the page does not say how to join

records.notes: The PACDC list gives germantownunitedcdc.org, which returned empty text on two tries. The working site is germantowncdc.org, found by search and fetched directly. The committees have no join steps. The get-involved page was not opened. Dated items on the home page: September 30, 2026, August 27, 2026 and August 24, 2026.

records.name: Southwest CDC
records.summary: A community group in Southwest Philadelphia that has served residents since 1987 with after-school, housing counseling and workforce services. Volunteers sign up by contacting the group's volunteer contact.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer by contacting the volunteer contact named on the volunteer page. The group also runs an after-school program and a Neighborhood Advisory Committee, with no schedules or join steps shown on the site.

schedule.text: No program schedules are shown. Volunteer sign-up is by contacting the volunteer contact.

first_step.how: Call or email the volunteer contact listed on the volunteer page
first_step.basis: Volunteering goes through a personal contact; no steps or schedule are shown

records.notes: The site has no dated items, so status is probably_active under the no-dates rule. The office line is 215-729-0800. The volunteer contact is a named staff member, published on the site as the volunteer line.

records.name: Jumpstart Tioga
records.summary: A group that helps Tioga residents become investors in their own neighborhood through real estate training, mentoring and help with financing.
records.what_you_do: Enroll in the 11th Real Estate Education Course (registration open, no start date shown). The group also offers a training program with mentoring and financing help, and a Facebook group where graduates, mentors and contractors share resources.

schedule.text: Course registration is open. Start dates and class times are not shown.

first_step.how: Use the course enrollment link on the group's site
first_step.basis: Enrollment comes before details; no price, start date or schedule is shown

records.notes: No dated items, so probably_active because the site works and enrollment is open. Recorded as a training program for residents, not a volunteer group. The enrollment page was not opened.

records.name: Oxford Circle Christian Community Development Association
records.summary: A faith-based community development group in Oxford Circle. It runs after-school and summer camp, food distribution, adult education, family resource centers and Parents as Teachers, and it welcomes volunteers.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer through the Volunteer Today link for roles working with adults and children, or with other tasks. Programs that may use volunteers include after-school and summer camp, food distribution, adult education and workforce, and Family Resource Centers. Times for each program are not shown.

schedule.text: Program times are not shown on the site. Volunteer roles are posted through the Volunteer Today link.

first_step.how: Use the Volunteer Today link on the group's site, or call (215) 288-8504
first_step.basis: Volunteer sign-up is public and a phone line is listed; schedules are not shown

records.notes: Faith-based (Christian) group. The denomination is not stated, so faith is 'other'. Its only dated item is a link to a 2021 summer camp, which is not a news item, so the status is unknown. Confirm before relying on it.

records.name: HACE CDC
records.summary: A community development group for Eastern North Philadelphia that works on affordable housing, support services and small business. Neighbors can join a monthly salsa event, a gardening club and summer block builds.
records.what_you_do: Come to the monthly Summer of Salsa at Fairhill Square. Volunteer on summer block builds with Rebuilding Together Philadelphia, or join the gardening club at the Mann Older Adult Center. The site also lists a neighborhood advisory committee, corridor cleaning and a main street program, with no join steps shown.

schedule.text: Summer of Salsa is monthly on the second Friday, 5 to 9 pm, at Fairhill Square (4th and Lehigh). Block build and garden dates are given only as June, with no year.

cost.text: Free tax prep for qualifying households is listed; event costs are not shown

first_step.how: Go to the monthly Summer of Salsa, or call 215-426-8025 to ask about volunteering
first_step.basis: The monthly event is public with a set time and place; volunteer steps are not shown

records.notes: The Summer of Salsa start date on the site is June 13, 2025. Block build and garden dates have no year, so they are not dated here. Tax prep and housing counseling are services, not volunteer roles. The events page was not opened.

records.name: Habitat for Humanity Philadelphia
records.summary: A housing nonprofit that builds and repairs homes with volunteers across Philadelphia and runs the ReStore. Individuals and groups can volunteer, and the page says all volunteers are welcome.
records.what_you_do: Start on the Individual Volunteering page, or join the Young Professionals volunteer network. A 2026 Construction Sprint on October 20 and a Habi Hour on October 29 are listed on the home page. Pope Leo Village, an interfaith effort to build 26 homes, has no sign-up steps shown.

schedule.text: Construction Sprint on October 20, 2026, and Habi Hour on October 29 (year shown in the event title). Build-day schedules are not shown on the page.

first_step.how: Start on the Individual Volunteering page, or call the office Monday to Friday, 9 am to 5 pm
first_step.basis: The page says all volunteers are welcome and points beginners to an individual volunteering page, though the steps are not spelled out

records.notes: Not a neighborhood CDC. Included because it is on the PACDC list and runs volunteer build days. The volunteer page does not describe a ReStore volunteer role or a build-day schedule, so none is claimed.

records.name: Rebuilding Together Philadelphia
records.summary: A nonprofit that makes free home repairs for homeowners who need them, with volunteer crews doing the work. Its block builds bring 100 to 250 volunteers to repair 10 to 15 homes in one area over two days.
records.what_you_do: Join a Block Build, held three times a year in April, June and October over two days. Each volunteer usually gives 7 to 8 hours on one day. Group and individual volunteers of all skill levels are welcome, and roles include general volunteer, house captain and skilled leader. Homeowners can request free repairs through the Get Repairs page.

schedule.text: Block Builds run in April, June and October as two-day events. The page gives no year for them.

cost.text: Homeowner repairs are free. The page does not state a cost for volunteers.

first_step.how: Email info@rebuildingphilly.org or call (215) 965-0777 to ask about the next Block Build, or check the events calendar
first_step.basis: All skill levels are welcome and the page lists a clear contact, though sign-up steps are not shown

records.notes: The volunteer page dates Block Builds only by month (April, June, October). Its footer year (2022) is not evidence, so the status is probably_active. Exact repair day dates are not shown.

records.name: Esperanza
records.summary: A faith-based nonprofit in the Hunting Park area of North Philadelphia. It runs youth leadership and music programs, housing and benefit help, job services and low-cost immigration legal help.
records.what_you_do: Join the Esperanza Youth Leadership Institute or the AMLA music classes for neighborhood youth, which are taught each year. Adults can get housing and benefit counseling, and anyone can use the Take Action page to get involved. Volunteer days and resident committees are not shown.

schedule.text: Program schedules are not shown on the site. The music classes are taught each year.

cost.text: Immigration legal help is described as low cost; other program costs are not shown

first_step.how: Use the Take Action page on the group's site, or call (215) 324-0746 to ask about youth programs
first_step.basis: Join steps for the youth institute and music classes are not shown

records.notes: Faith-based, with no tradition named, so faith is 'other'. The 2026 date comes from a news item whose body gives August 11, 2026; the listing shows only month and day. Program join steps are not shown.

records.name: SEAMAAC
aka: Southeast Asian Mutual Assistance Associations Coalition
records.summary: A nonprofit that has helped immigrant and refugee families in Greater Philadelphia since 1984. Teens can join an afternoon arts program at Furness High School, and volunteers can use the group's volunteer page.
records.what_you_do: Join the Urban Arts Entrepreneurship program after school at Furness High School, with classes in breakdancing, deejaying, music production and visual arts. Volunteer through the volunteer page. Health and social services and a Mifflin Square Park project are also listed, with no join steps shown.

schedule.text: Urban Arts Entrepreneurship program at Furness High School, Monday to Friday, 2:30 to 5 pm. Summer dates and sign-up are not shown.

first_step.how: Youth can join through the program page linked from the home page; volunteers use the volunteer page
first_step.basis: The join route is linked, but the home page shows no steps or dates

records.notes: The only date on the site is a 2021 copyright footer, which is not evidence, so the status is probably_active. The program page was not opened, and the school's street address is not shown.

records.name: Asociación Puertorriqueños en Marcha (APM)
records.summary: A Latino-based nonprofit in Philadelphia that provides family, health, behavioral health, and community and economic development services. Its volunteer teams help with community clean-ups, paint days and festivals.
records.what_you_do: Fill in the online volunteer form for areas such as community clean-ups and paint days, the Sugar Cane Festival, the holiday toy drive, the Puerto Rican Day Parade and the annual gala. The page says some placements may need a background check.

schedule.text: Volunteer dates are not shown. The 2026 Sugar Cane Festival and the 2026 Gift of Love children's benefit are listed by name.

first_step.how: Fill in the online volunteer form on the APM volunteer page (name and email are required)
first_step.basis: The volunteer form is public and short, but the page does not show event dates

records.notes: The volunteer page says opportunities may be limited due to COVID-19, an older note that may be out of date. The status date comes from the home page's July 7, 2026 board news. The 2026 festival and benefit names appear in menu titles only.

records.name: Neighborhood Gardens Trust
records.summary: A Philadelphia group that supports community gardens. It keeps a garden map so residents can find a garden to join, though many gardens have waiting lists.
records.what_you_do: Find a community garden on the garden map, open its More Info section for the best contact, and ask about a plot. Demand is high and many gardens have waitlists. The site does not describe volunteer work days.

schedule.text: Each garden sets its own days. The site lists no work days or meetings.

first_step.how: Open the garden map on the site, find a garden, and click More Info for its contact; or email ngt@pennhort.org for help
first_step.basis: The steps are clear, but many gardens have waitlists

records.notes: A support organization for gardens rather than a CDC, included because it is on the PACDC list and its garden map is a way for residents to join. No dated items, so probably_active under the no-dates rule.

records.name: African Cultural Alliance of North America (ACANA)
records.summary: A Philadelphia group that helps refugees, immigrant families and other residents reach legal, health and social services. It runs digital literacy classes, health screenings and job training, and it works on African arts and culture.
records.what_you_do: Take a digital literacy class (day, evening and weekend sessions may be possible), or join a free construction training course (NCCER pre-apprenticeship, about 10 weeks, enrolling for fall 2026). Free health events are also listed, including a hepatitis B screening for people over 16.

schedule.text: Digital literacy classes run on a flexible schedule. Listed dates: a hepatitis B screening on September 24, 2026, and a construction training open house on October 16, 2026, 10 am to noon.

cost.text: Several listed events are free; class costs are not shown

first_step.how: Call (215) 729-8225 or email info@acanaus.org and ask about the digital literacy classes
first_step.basis: Classes are public with a phone line and email; enrollment steps are not shown

records.notes: A named program contact is on the site and is not recorded; the office line is used. The 'over 16' rule applies to the hepatitis B screening only. The get-involved and events pages were not opened.

notes: Searches: 3 of 3 used. Fetches: 59 of 60 used, including the two PACDC pages. The PACDC members list has about 157 names. Most are banks, lenders, architects, contractors, consultants, hospitals, funders and housing developers with no resident program, so they are not recorded. Records here are neighborhood CDCs, business districts, and volunteer or service groups that name a program a resident can join. Checked and dropped for no joinable program shown: Centennial Parkside CDC (newest dated item 2023), Frankford CDC (only an event calendar), Tacony CDC (newest dated item April 2025, programs page lists none), PassyARC (a sidewalk cleaning program with no join steps), South Kensington Community Partners (no programs listed), MECCA (program names only, no join steps, no dated items), Tioga United (past clean-ups only, office by appointment), Community of Compassion CDC (newest dated item February 2023), Sister Clara Muhammad CDC (no programs), ICPIC New Africa Center CDC (newest dated items 2021), LA21, Old City District, Park to Broad and South Street Headhouse (business services only, no resident volunteer path), WCRP (housing applications only), Impact Services (no programs described), ProjectHOME (volunteer page has no details, only a race registration), Called To Serve CDC (generic volunteer line with no named program; worth revisiting), and TURN Tenant Union Representative Network (hotline and workshops listed, but newest dated item January 2024, so dormant under the date rule; worth a fresh check). Newbold CDC: the listed site redirects to an unrelated domain, which was not followed; a 2014 article describes a Newbold CDC corridor-cleaning program; no current site was found; dropped. WORC (Wynnefield Overbrook Revitalization) redirects to a university home page, not followed; dropped. Empowered CDC and Northwest CLT returned 404 on the homepage; dropped. Heritage CDC: see leads_only. Germantown United CDC: the list's germantownunitedcdc.org returned empty text twice; the working site is germantowncdc.org, found by search. Chestnut Hill: the list calls it Chestnut Hill CDC; its own site is the Chestnut Hill Business District, recorded under that name with the old one as an alias. New Kensington CDC: the www host has a certificate error; the record uses nkcdc.org. Sign-up paths that run through third-party sign-in or registration forms (Nicetown CDC volunteer link, Xiente register links) were not used. Faith: OCCCDA and Esperanza call themselves faith-based without naming a tradition, so audience.faith is 'other'. Undated items: some sites give months or days with no year (Autumn on the Avenue, the Cresheim clean-up, Rebuilding Together block builds, HACE block build and garden dates, NKCDC parent workshops), and these are not dated in the records. OCCCDA status is unknown because its only dated item is a 2021 camp link. Probably_active is used for working sites with no dates (Southwest CDC, Jumpstart Tioga, Rebuilding Together, SEAMAAC, Neighborhood Gardens Trust). A named staff volunteer contact is recorded only for Southwest CDC, as published. Habitat for Humanity and Neighborhood Gardens Trust are included as PACDC members that run volunteer days or garden joining, though they are not neighborhood CDCs. Habitat's ReStore volunteer role is not claimed. The leads_only list holds PACDC members that were not fetched because the budget ran out; they should be checked in a later wave.
